chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Khalid ibn Jarir from Abu al-Rabii al-Shami from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who takes land from the landowners (dehqans) and rents it out for more than what he paid for it, and pays the ruler's share (tax) from it. He said, 'There is no harm with it, for the land is not like the hired worker, nor like the house; for the surplus/profit of the hired worker and the house is forbidden (when rented out for more than paid).'

key_terms.يَتَقَبَّلُ: To take/accept (in the context of leasing or taking possession)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to rent land from a landowner and sub-lease it for a profit in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes agricultural land from movable assets like hired laborers or houses, permitting the lessee to sub-lease for a profit margin exceeding the original cost. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that land is a productive asset where value addition is inherent, contrasting with the fixed nature of labor or housing rents. It provides a foundational basis for modern agricultural leasing and investment structures in Islamic finance.
